listening.title: Team meeting — vendor contract renewal decision
listening.speaker: Priya (Procurement) ↔ Tom (Operations) ↔ Nadia (Finance)
listening.transcript:
PRIYA: Thanks for jumping on this. We need to decide on the Meridian Logistics contract before Friday, since their current agreement expires end of month. Tom, what's your read from the operations side?
TOM: Honestly, mixed. Their on-time delivery rate has been solid, 97% over the last two quarters, but their customer service response time has gotten worse — we've had three separate incidents where it took over 48 hours to get a reply about a delayed shipment.
PRIYA: That matches what I'm seeing too. Nadia, what does the renewal actually cost us compared to switching?
NADIA: The renewal as written raises our monthly rate by 12%, mostly citing fuel costs. If we switch to Harborline, their quote is actually 5% lower than what we currently pay, not just lower than Meridian's new rate, but the catch is they can't onboard until at least six weeks out, and Tom, you mentioned we have that holiday shipping surge starting in five weeks.
TOM: Right, that's the real problem. If we switch, we'd have maybe a one-week gap where Harborline isn't ready but our current contract with Meridian would have already ended. That's not something we can risk during peak season.
PRIYA: So it sounds like a straight switch right now is too risky, but staying at the new 12% rate isn't great either.
NADIA: There's actually a third option I want to float. We could sign a short-term, three-month extension with Meridian at their new rate specifically to bridge the surge period, then switch to Harborline once that extension ends, once they're fully onboarded and there's no gap.
TOM: I like that in theory, but would Meridian even agree to a short extension instead of the full annual renewal they're pushing for?
PRIYA: I can find out — I spoke with their account rep last week and got the sense they're more worried about losing us entirely than about contract length specifically.
NADIA: If Priya can get that shorter deal, my recommendation is to do exactly that: three-month bridge with Meridian, then transition to Harborline, since the long-term savings make up for the short-term extra cost within about four months.
TOM: I can support that, as long as the transition timeline is documented and Harborline's onboarding doesn't slip further.
PRIYA: Agreed. I'll call the Meridian rep this afternoon and report back by tomorrow morning. If they won't budge on a short-term deal, we'll need to reconvene and reconsider the full annual renewal instead, since we can't risk the surge period regardless.

questions.explanation: Priya says the decision is needed 'since their current agreement expires end of month.'

questions.explanation: Tom cites 'three separate incidents where it took over 48 hours to get a reply.'

questions.explanation: Nadia says the renewal 'raises our monthly rate by 12%.'

questions.explanation: Nadia says the increase is cited as 'mostly citing fuel costs.'

questions.explanation: Nadia clarifies Harborline's quote is '5% lower than what we currently pay, not just lower than Meridian's new rate.'

questions.label: Question 7
questions.question: What is the main drawback of switching to Harborline immediately?
options: Their delivery rate is worse than Meridian's
They can't onboard for at least six weeks, creating a gap during the holiday surge

questions.explanation: Harborline 'can't onboard until at least six weeks out,' which conflicts with the surge starting in five weeks, creating a coverage gap.

options: In three weeks

questions.explanation: Nadia references 'that holiday shipping surge starting in five weeks,' which Tom confirms.

questions.explanation: Tom asks 'would Meridian even agree to a short extension instead of the full annual renewal they're pushing for?'

questions.explanation: Tom supports the plan 'as long as the transition timeline is documented and Harborline's onboarding doesn't slip further.'

options: Sign the Harborline contract today
Call the Meridian account rep this afternoon and report back by tomorrow morning

questions.explanation: Priya says 'I'll call the Meridian rep this afternoon and report back by tomorrow morning.'

questions.label: Question 15
questions.question: If Meridian refuses a short-term deal, what does the group agree to do, and why?
options: Switch to Harborline anyway and accept the coverage gap
Reconvene and likely accept the full annual renewal, since the surge period risk cannot be taken regardless
Cancel Meridian's contract immediately with no replacement
Delay the entire decision until after the holiday surge
questions.explanation: Priya states that if Meridian won't budge, they'll 'reconvene and reconsider the full annual renewal instead, since we can't risk the surge period regardless' — tying back to Tom's earlier point about the unacceptable risk of a coverage gap.

reading.title: Double correspondence — freelancer invoice dispute and policy reference
reading.passage:
EMAIL 1: Freelancer to Client (October 14)

Subject: Invoice #2231 — Payment Status

Hi Marcus,

I'm following up on Invoice #2231 for the website copywriting project, submitted September 28. Per our agreement, payment is due within 15 business days of submission, which would have made the deadline October 20. However, I noticed your company's contractor portal shows a separate "net-30 calendar days" policy for all invoices over $2,000, and my invoice total is $2,400.

I want to make sure I understand which timeline applies here, since the two policies seem to conflict, and I'd rather clarify now than assume incorrectly. Also, a smaller note: I revised the homepage section twice at your team's request after initial submission — do those revisions reset the invoice date, or does the clock still run from the original September 28 submission?

Could you confirm with your finance team and let me know? I don't want to send a formal late notice prematurely if I'm simply misunderstanding the applicable policy.

Thanks,
Elena

---

EMAIL 2: Client's Finance Team to Freelancer (October 16)

Subject: RE: Invoice #2231 — Payment Status

Hi Elena,

Thanks for flagging this, and apologies for the confusing overlap in our documentation — we're aware the contractor portal language needs updating. Here's the clarification: the 15-business-day term in your contract applies to standard invoices, but our net-30-calendar-day policy specifically overrides that for any invoice at or above $2,000, precisely because larger invoices require an additional internal budget sign-off step that shorter timelines don't accommodate. Since your invoice is $2,400, the net-30 policy applies, not the 15-business-day term.

Regarding your revision question: per our contractor handbook, revisions requested within 10 days of original submission do not reset the invoice date, but revisions requested after that 10-day window do reset the clock to the date the final revision was delivered. Your first revision request came on October 3, which is within that 10-day window from your September 28 submission, so it does not affect the date. However, I don't see a record of a second revision request in our system — could you confirm the date of that second request, since if it fell outside the 10-day window, the clock would reset accordingly?

Once we confirm that, we'll calculate the exact due date and process payment shortly after. Thanks for your patience.

Best,
Daniel, Finance Team
